goals.name: iOS Developer Interview Preparation
goals.description: Get ready for mid-level iOS interviews: Swift memory and concurrency, SwiftUI, coding problems, and a mock interview.

phases.name: Swift Fundamentals
phases.description: Memory management and concurrency, the topics most iOS interviews probe first.

phases.name: SwiftUI
phases.description: How SwiftUI tracks identity and state, and enough hands-on building to talk about it with confidence.

phases.name: Interview Practice
phases.description: Coding problems, common iOS questions, and a timed mock interview.

resources.title: Automatic Reference Counting (The Swift Programming Language)
resources.notes: Know strong reference cycles and when to use weak versus unowned, including in closures.

resources.title: Concurrency (The Swift Programming Language)
resources.notes: Focus on tasks, task groups, actors and Sendable. Be ready to explain data races.

resources.title: Meet async/await in Swift (WWDC21)
resources.notes: Watch how completion handlers become async functions. A common whiteboard question.

resources.title: Demystify SwiftUI (WWDC21)
resources.notes: Identity, lifetime and dependencies: the basis for answering why a view redraws or loses state.

resources.title: 100 Days of SwiftUI (Hacking with Swift)
resources.notes: Free. Budget for the projects and consolidation days you need, not all 100 days.

resources.title: NeetCode Practice
resources.notes: Work through arrays, hashing, two pointers, trees and graphs. Solve in Swift, out loud.

resources.title: iOS Interview Questions (Hacking with Swift)
resources.notes: Answer each question aloud before reading the hints, as you would in the interview.

resources.title: Mock interview on interviewing.io
resources.notes: Book one timed mock in the last two weeks. Some sessions are paid.
